# Voice (area `voice`)

Push-to-talk, hearing and speech on the daemon side.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **VOICE-400** (owner): Setting up push-to-talk happens in FERB.app; there is no CLI path for it (no `ferb setup --voice`, no `ferb voice`).
- **VOICE-401** (owner): FERB speaks with macOS's native voice and dictates with the app's dictation. Other text-to-speech providers plug in later like the runtime adapters. Local human-like voices (Kokoro, Chatterbox) and a local dictation engine (Parakeet/Whisper with clean-up) are deferred until the owner raises them.
- **VOICE-403** (owner): The one push-to-talk path is the app's dictation (hold Right Command + Option, the Mac's language), with an option to send on release; replies are spoken through the pluggable speaker; the daemon has no push-to-talk stack. The FERB Voice helper is merged into FERB.app: FERB.app itself answers `transcribe`, `status` and `request-speech` for hearing, and Speech Recognition is one grant for dictation and hearing.
- **VOICE-404** (agent): Any new message, typed or spoken, `task.stop` (whatever ids) and the global stop interrupt what FERB is saying; the daemon's shutdown ends it. Within one turn, utterances queue in order (plan line, then the answer) rather than cutting each other off.
- **VOICE-405** (agent): A turn sent with `speak: true` speaks its reply, its task's plan line (not again for a resumed task) and the answer, without code's lines after them (sites contacted, schedules, apps left open). Questions FERB asks during a voice task are not spoken; they show in the notch. A spoken message merged into an earlier turn makes that turn spoken. Words come from structured events, never CLI rendering.
- **VOICE-406** (agent): `Speech.say` redacts the raw text, reshapes it for speech (`spoken`), then redacts again, before any provider is built; no provider, hosted or local, can receive unredacted text and none needs a flag. `voice.said` and `voice.failed` carry only redacted words.
- **VOICE-407** (agent): `PROVIDERS` in ferb/voice/speak.py is the registry, like the runtime catalog: `[voice] tts` (default "macos"), `voice`, `rate`. A provider is built per utterance, so an edit applies to the next one without a restart; a bad value is journaled `voice.failed` once per turn's queue and nothing is spoken. `MacVoice` passes the text to `/usr/bin/say` on stdin, never argv.
- **VOICE-408** (agent): `[voice] rate` is checked only as a positive finite number of words per minute; `voice` only for shape (non-empty, not option-like, no control characters). A voice macOS doesn't know makes `say` fail, journaled.
